originalTitle: ‘Super El Niño’ could bring wet winter and flooding to western US, climate scientists warn
summary: Weather system tied to warming sea surface expected to intensify in fall and winter, persisting until early spring 2027
content: El Niño, a recurring climate phenomenon marked by above-average sea surface temperatures, when changes in wind patterns allow warmer water to spread across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, could spell a wet winter for portions of the western and south-eastern US, climate models show. Coastal areas may be at elevated risk of flooding, experts warn. Climate scientists predict this year’s “super” El Niño, a label assigned when sea surface temperatures climb by at least 2C, will be the strongest of the century. The weather system is expected to intensify in the fall and winter, persisting until early spring 2027, according to the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa). California has a 70%-100% chance of experiencing above-average rainfall along its coast, according to a model from the European center for medium-range forecasts. “El Niño is never going to guarantee any particular outcome in any California winter,” Daniel Swain, the UCLA climate scientist, noted at a virtual El Niño town hall hosted by the California state senator Mike McGuire this week. But, he added, a weather event as strong as the one being currently predicted shifts the odds in favor of a wet winter: “That will likely affect and increase the likelihood of coastal flooding, particularly during strong storm events or during king tide events.” California has been devastated by El Niños in the past. A 1982-83 weather system destroyed 33 oceanfront homes and damaged 3,000 other residences, according to the California coastal commission. In a 1997-98 El Niño, California experienced massive flooding and 17 storm-related deaths. In more recent history, during the El Niño winter of 2015-16, state officials reported record coastal erosion on California beaches. “With less beach in front of the coastline, the waves will have even greater impact on the shoreline with more likelihood of flooding and undercutting of cliffs,” said Mark Merrifield of the Scripps Institution of Oceanography, at McGuire’s town hall. El Niño is not expected to completely erase drought in the US south-west, where some reservoirs are at an all-time low. “It would have to be exceptionally wet,” Dr Joel Lisonbee, senior associate scientist at the Cooperative Institute for Research in Environmental Sciences at the University of Colorado Boulder, told the Guardian in June. “That would also mean flooding, and the destruction and potential loss of life that comes along with that.” Swathes of the US Gulf coast and east coast, stretching from Florida up to the mid-Atlantic region, are facing similar high odds of increased precipitation. During El Niño years, central and south Florida has historically experienced more severe weather with more tornadoes and flood events, according to Noaa. In a 1998 El Niño winter, an outbreak of unusually strong tornadoes in that region led to 42 deaths and more than $100m in damage. Experts warn that not every El Niño behaves the same, nor does it affect different geographical regions in the same way. Some have fueled hurricanes and heavy precipitation, while others have triggered extreme heat and drought. While this is “a natural cycle”, Merrifield said at the town hall, the potential effects of a temporary sea-level rise in California from the super El Niño also “gives us a bit of a stress test of what the state is likely to experience with future climate change”. “The El Niño, I think, is a good opportunity to sort of see where our vulnerabilities are throughout the state and what we can do to prepare,” Merrifield added, “and it also is a sobering look at what we can expect with climate change.”
chineseTitle: 气候科学家警告称，“超级厄尔尼诺”可能会给美国西部带来潮湿的冬季和洪水
chineseSummary: 与海面变暖相关的天气系统预计将在秋季和冬季加剧，并持续到 2027 年初春
chineseContent: 气候模型显示，厄尔尼诺现象是一种反复出现的气候现象，其特征是海面温度高于平均水平，当风型的变化使温暖的海水扩散到赤道太平洋中部和东部时，可能会给美国西部和东南部部分地区带来潮湿的冬季。专家警告说，沿海地区发生洪水的风险可能较高。气候科学家预测，今年的“超级”厄尔尼诺现象（当海面温度上升至少 2 摄氏度时就会被贴上标签）将是本世纪最强的厄尔尼诺现象。据美国国家海洋和大气管理局 (Noaa) 称，预计该天气系统将在秋季和冬季加强，一直持续到 2027 年初春。根据欧洲中期预测中心的模型，加利福尼亚州沿海地区的降雨量有 70%-100% 的可能性高于平均水平。加州大学洛杉矶分校气候科学家丹尼尔·斯温本周在加利福尼亚州参议员迈克·麦奎尔主持的虚拟厄尔尼诺市政厅上指出：“厄尔尼诺现象永远不会保证加州的任何一个冬天都会出现任何特定的结果。”但是，他补充说，像目前预测的那样强烈的天气事件会改变潮湿冬季的可能性：“这可能会影响并增加沿海洪水的可能性，特别是在强风暴事件或大潮事件期间。”加利福尼亚州过去曾遭受过厄尔尼诺现象的破坏。据加州海岸委员会称，1982-83 年的天气系统摧毁了 33 座海滨房屋，并损坏了 3,000 座其他住宅。在 1997-98 年的厄尔尼诺现象中，加利福尼亚州经历了大规模洪水，造成 17 人因风暴死亡。在最近的历史中，2015-16 年厄尔尼诺现象冬季期间，州官员报告称，加州海滩出现了创纪录的海岸侵蚀。 “FR 的海滩较少
